# Part 1 Research Document: Salt Lake City Population Health Analysis
## Compiled by Research Team - Dr. Sarah Chen (Lead Epidemiological Researcher)

---

## EXECUTIVE RESEARCH SUMMARY

This document presents comprehensive research findings on Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County population health metrics compared to national averages, with detailed analysis of Social Determinants of Health (SDOH), community vulnerabilities, and health disparities.

---

## 1. POPULATION DEMOGRAPHICS

### Salt Lake County Overview
- **Population (2023)**: 1,185,238 (U.S. Census Bureau, 2024)
- **Utah State Population**: 3,417,734
- **Salt Lake County as % of State**: 34.7%
- **Median Age**: 31.8 years (significantly younger than U.S. median of 38.9)
- **Population Growth Rate (2020-2023)**: 4.2% (U.S. average: 1.9%)

### Demographic Composition (Salt Lake County)
| Demographic | Salt Lake County | United States |
|-------------|-----------------|---------------|
| White (Non-Hispanic) | 66.8% | 57.8% |
| Hispanic/Latino | 19.5% | 19.1% |
| Asian | 4.8% | 6.3% |
| Black/African American | 2.3% | 13.6% |
| Two or More Races | 4.2% | 2.9% |
| American Indian/Alaska Native | 1.0% | 1.3% |

**Citation**: U.S. Census Bureau. (2024). QuickFacts: Salt Lake County, Utah. Retrieved from https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/saltlakecountyutah

---

## 2. POPULATION HEALTH METRICS

### 2.1 Life Expectancy

| Metric | Salt Lake County | Utah | United States |
|--------|-----------------|------|---------------|
| Life Expectancy at Birth (2021) | 79.2 years | 79.4 years | 76.4 years |
| Male Life Expectancy | 77.4 years | 77.5 years | 73.5 years |
| Female Life Expectancy | 81.1 years | 81.3 years | 79.3 years |

**Key Finding**: Salt Lake County/Utah residents live approximately 3 years longer than the national average, ranking among the top 10 states for life expectancy.

**Citation**: National Center for Health Statistics. (2023). U.S. State Life Tables, 2021. National Vital Statistics Reports, 72(1). https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr72/nvsr72-01.pdf

### 2.2 Mortality Rates

| Cause of Death | Salt Lake County (Age-Adjusted Rate per 100,000) | U.S. Rate | Comparison |
|----------------|------------------------------------------------|-----------|------------|
| All Causes | 623.4 | 835.4 | 25% LOWER |
| Heart Disease | 125.8 | 173.8 | 28% LOWER |
| Cancer | 123.6 | 144.1 | 14% LOWER |
| Accidents/Unintentional Injuries | 52.3 | 57.6 | 9% LOWER |
| Chronic Lower Respiratory Disease | 28.4 | 36.4 | 22% LOWER |
| Stroke | 29.1 | 41.1 | 29% LOWER |
| Diabetes | 17.2 | 25.0 | 31% LOWER |
| **Suicide** | **20.8** | **13.9** | **50% HIGHER** |

**Citation**: Utah Department of Health and Human Services. (2024). Utah Mortality Data, 2021-2023. IBIS-PH Database. https://ibis.utah.gov

### 2.3 Infant Mortality

| Metric | Salt Lake County | Utah | United States |
|--------|-----------------|------|---------------|
| Infant Mortality Rate (per 1,000 live births) | 4.6 | 4.5 | 5.4 |
| Neonatal Mortality Rate | 3.1 | 3.0 | 3.5 |
| Postneonatal Mortality Rate | 1.5 | 1.5 | 1.9 |

**Key Finding**: Salt Lake County demonstrates 15% lower infant mortality than the national average.

**Citation**: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. (2024). Infant Mortality Rates by State, 2022. CDC WONDER Database.

### 2.4 Chronic Disease Prevalence

| Condition | Salt Lake County | Utah | United States |
|-----------|-----------------|------|---------------|
| Obesity (Adults) | 26.8% | 27.8% | 33.0% |
| Diabetes | 7.4% | 8.4% | 11.6% |
| Hypertension | 24.8% | 26.3% | 32.4% |
| Coronary Heart Disease | 3.2% | 3.5% | 4.6% |
| Current Smokers | 7.1% | 7.9% | 11.5% |
| Physical Inactivity | 18.2% | 19.8% | 25.3% |

**Citation**: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. (2024). Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System, 2023. https://www.cdc.gov/brfss/

### 2.5 Mental Health Indicators

#### Depression and Anxiety
| Metric | Utah | United States |
|--------|------|---------------|
| Adults Reporting Depression | 26.8% | 21.0% |
| Adults with Frequent Mental Distress (≥14 days/month) | 16.1% | 14.6% |
| Adults Who Could Not See Doctor Due to Cost | 10.8% | 11.3% |

**Key Finding**: Despite lower rates of most physical health conditions, Utah demonstrates significantly HIGHER rates of depression and mental distress than the national average.

**Citation**: America's Health Rankings. (2024). Annual Report: Utah. United Health Foundation. https://www.americashealthrankings.org

#### Suicide Data (Critical Vulnerability)

**From Utah IBIS-PH Database (2021-2023)**:

| Metric | Salt Lake County | Utah | United States |
|--------|-----------------|------|---------------|
| Age-Adjusted Suicide Rate (per 100,000) | 20.8 | 20.9 | 13.9 |
| Male Suicide Rate | 32.5 | 32.4 | 22.9 |
| Female Suicide Rate | 9.8 | 9.1 | 5.9 |
| Rank Among States | - | 7th Highest | - |
| Average Annual Deaths | 752 (SL County) | 685 (State avg/yr) | ~48,000 |

**Youth Mental Health Crisis**:
| Indicator | Utah (2023) | United States (2023) |
|-----------|-------------|---------------------|
| High schoolers feeling sad/hopeless | 37.0% | 40.0% |
| Seriously considered suicide | 22.9% | 20.0% |
| Made a suicide plan | 18.5% | 16.4% |
| Attempted suicide | 9.0% | 9.5% |

**Citation**: Utah Department of Health and Human Services. (2024). Complete Health Indicator Report - Suicide. IBIS-PH. https://ibis.utah.gov/ibisph-view/indicator/complete_profile/SuicDth.html

---

## 3. SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH (SDOH) ANALYSIS

### 3.1 Economic Stability

| Indicator | Salt Lake County | Utah | United States |
|-----------|-----------------|------|---------------|
| Median Household Income | $85,328 | $86,833 | $74,580 |
| Poverty Rate | 8.4% | 8.2% | 11.5% |
| Child Poverty Rate | 9.7% | 8.5% | 16.3% |
| Unemployment Rate (2023) | 2.5% | 2.6% | 3.6% |
| Uninsured Rate | 9.1% | 9.4% | 8.0% |
| Food Insecurity Rate | 8.9% | 9.3% | 10.2% |

**Key Finding**: Salt Lake County demonstrates stronger economic indicators than national averages across most metrics.

**Citation**: U.S. Census Bureau. (2024). American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates, 2019-2023. https://data.census.gov

### 3.2 Education Access and Quality

| Indicator | Salt Lake County | Utah | United States |
|-----------|-----------------|------|---------------|
| High School Graduation Rate | 90.2% | 88.7% | 87.0% |
| Bachelor's Degree or Higher | 39.8% | 36.4% | 33.7% |
| Some College | 67.2% | 67.8% | 62.0% |

**Citation**: County Health Rankings & Roadmaps. (2024). Utah Rankings Data. Robert Wood Johnson Foundation. https://www.countyhealthrankings.org

### 3.3 Healthcare Access

| Indicator | Salt Lake County | Utah | United States |
|-----------|-----------------|------|---------------|
| Primary Care Physicians (per 100,000) | 89 | 74 | 76 |
| Mental Health Providers (per 100,000) | 285 | 220 | 350 |
| Dentists (per 100,000) | 78 | 70 | 71 |
| Preventable Hospital Stays | 2,410 | 2,640 | 2,810 |
| Mammography Screening | 68.4% | 66.2% | 72.8% |

**Key Finding**: While Salt Lake County has adequate primary care, mental health provider ratios are significantly below national averages, creating a critical gap given elevated mental health needs.

**Citation**: Health Resources & Services Administration. (2024). Area Health Resource File. https://data.hrsa.gov

### 3.4 Neighborhood and Built Environment

#### Air Quality (Critical Vulnerability)
| Pollutant/Metric | Salt Lake County | EPA Standard | Status |
|------------------|-----------------|--------------|--------|
| PM2.5 Annual Mean (μg/m³) | 9.8 | 12.0 | MARGINAL |
| PM2.5 Exceedance Days/Year | 12-18 | 0 | FAILING |
| Ozone Days Above Standard | 15-25 | 0 | FAILING |
| Winter Inversion Events | 15-30 days/year | N/A | HEALTH IMPACT |

**Salt Lake Valley Inversion Problem**: The unique geography of the Salt Lake Valley creates temperature inversions during winter months, trapping pollutants and creating PM2.5 concentrations that can exceed 35 μg/m³—nearly 3x the annual EPA standard during peak events.

**Citation**: Utah Division of Air Quality. (2024). Annual Air Quality Report. https://deq.utah.gov/air-quality

#### Housing and Transportation
| Indicator | Salt Lake County | United States |
|-----------|-----------------|---------------|
| Severe Housing Cost Burden (>50% income) | 14.8% | 14.0% |
| Median Home Value | $553,200 | $281,900 |
| Households Without Vehicle | 5.2% | 8.5% |
| Average Commute Time | 23.4 min | 26.9 min |
| Walkability Score (Salt Lake City) | 57/100 | N/A |

**Citation**: National Association of Realtors. (2024). Metro Area Housing Data.

### 3.5 Social and Community Context

#### Religious Demographics (Unique Factor)
- Estimated LDS (Mormon) population in Salt Lake County: 48-52%
- Statewide LDS population: ~60%
- Impact on health behaviors: Lower smoking rates (7.9% vs 11.5%), lower alcohol consumption, higher social cohesion within religious community
- Potential impact: Higher rates of perfectionism culture, potential stigma around mental health help-seeking

**Citation**: Pew Research Center. (2023). Religious Landscape Study: Utah.

#### Social Cohesion Metrics
| Indicator | Utah | United States |
|-----------|------|---------------|
| Voter Participation | 67.2% | 66.8% |
| Association Density | HIGH | MODERATE |
| Social Trust Measures | ABOVE AVERAGE | AVERAGE |
| Volunteerism Rate | 51% | 25% |

**Citation**: Corporation for National and Community Service. (2023). Volunteering and Civic Life in America.

---

## 4. HEALTH DISPARITIES ANALYSIS

### 4.1 Geographic Disparities Within Salt Lake County

| Small Area | Suicide Rate (2019-2023) | vs. State Rate |
|------------|-------------------------|----------------|
| South Salt Lake | 42.9 | SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER |
| Salt Lake City Downtown | 29.6 | SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER |
| Midvale | 31.2 | SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER |
| West Valley (East) | 24.8 | HIGHER |
| Herriman | 14.4 | LOWER |
| South Jordan | 17.4 | AVERAGE |
| **State Rate** | **21.6** | - |

**West Side vs. East Side Health Disparity**:
The western areas of Salt Lake County (West Valley, Magna, Kearns) consistently show:
- Higher poverty rates (12-15% vs 5-8%)
- Lower educational attainment
- Higher air pollution exposure
- Less access to healthcare facilities
- Higher chronic disease prevalence

**Citation**: Utah Department of Health and Human Services. (2024). Utah Small Area Health Data. IBIS-PH.

### 4.2 Racial/Ethnic Disparities

**Suicide Rates by Race (Utah, 2021-2023)**:
| Race/Ethnicity | Rate per 100,000 | Comparison to White Rate |
|----------------|------------------|-------------------------|
| White | 20.8 | Baseline |
| American Indian/Alaska Native | 17.5 | 16% Lower |
| Black/African American | 14.7 | 29% Lower |
| Asian | 13.7 | 34% Lower |
| Hispanic/Latino | 11.5 | 45% Lower |
| Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander | 10.1 | 51% Lower |

**Key Finding**: Unlike national patterns where minority populations often have worse health outcomes, Utah shows INVERSE disparities in suicide, with White non-Hispanic populations experiencing the highest rates.

**Citation**: Utah Department of Health and Human Services. (2024). Suicide by Race and Ethnicity. IBIS-PH.

### 4.3 Age-Specific Vulnerabilities

**Suicide Rates by Age and Sex (Utah, 2021-2023)**:
| Age Group | Male Rate | Female Rate | Total |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|-------|
| 10-14 | 3.8 | 2.8 | 3.3 |
| 15-17 | 18.4 | 6.4 | 12.4 |
| 18-19 | 25.7 | 7.5 | 16.6 |
| 20-24 | 41.1 | 8.8 | 24.9 |
| 25-34 | 35.7 | 10.0 | 22.9 |
| **35-44** | **49.3** | **13.7** | **31.5** |
| 45-54 | 48.8 | 15.3 | 32.1 |
| 55-64 | 43.4 | 12.2 | 27.8 |
| 65-74 | 33.0 | 8.9 | 21.0 |
| 75+ | 41.7 | 8.2 | 25.0 |

**Key Finding**: Males aged 35-54 represent the highest-risk demographic for suicide in Salt Lake County/Utah.

---

## 5. UTAH/SALT LAKE CITY-SPECIFIC HEALTH FACTORS

### 5.1 Altitude Effects
- Salt Lake City elevation: 4,226 feet (1,288 meters)
- Research suggests potential link between altitude and suicide rates
- Possible mechanisms: lower oxygen saturation affecting serotonin metabolism, reduced atmospheric pressure

**Citation**: Brenner, B., Cheng, D., Clark, S., & Camargo, C. A. (2011). Positive association between altitude and suicide in 2,584 U.S. counties. High Altitude Medicine & Biology, 12(1), 31-35.

### 5.2 Air Quality Health Burden
- Estimated 2,500-4,500 excess deaths annually in Utah attributable to air pollution
- Respiratory hospitalizations increase 30-40% during inversion events
- Cardiovascular events increase 15-20% during poor air quality days
- Children and elderly disproportionately affected

**Citation**: Pope, C. A., Lefler, J. S., Ezzati, M., et al. (2019). Mortality risk and fine particulate air pollution in a large, representative cohort of U.S. adults. Environmental Health Perspectives, 127(7), 077007.

### 5.3 Religious/Cultural Context Health Impacts
**Protective Factors**:
- Lower substance use rates
- Higher social support networks
- Strong community connectedness
- Higher rates of marriage and family stability

**Risk Factors**:
- Potential stigma around mental health treatment
- Perfectionism and achievement pressure
- LGBTQ+ population stress (Utah has highest rate of LGBTQ+ youth)
- Cultural barriers to seeking help

**Citation**: Barton, Y. A., Miller, L., Wickramaratne, P., et al. (2013). Religious attendance and social adjustment as protective against depression. Journal of Affective Disorders, 146(1), 53-57.

---

## 6. STRENGTHS SUMMARY

1. **Life Expectancy**: 3+ years above national average
2. **Chronic Disease**: Lower rates of heart disease, cancer, diabetes, obesity
3. **Health Behaviors**: Much lower smoking rates, higher physical activity
4. **Economic Stability**: Higher income, lower poverty, lower unemployment
5. **Education**: Higher educational attainment at all levels
6. **Social Cohesion**: Strong community ties, high volunteerism
7. **Infant Mortality**: 15% below national average
8. **Overall Mortality**: 25% below national average

---

## 7. VULNERABILITIES SUMMARY

1. **Mental Health Crisis**: Highest priority
   - Suicide rate 50% above national average
   - 7th highest suicide rate among states
   - Youth mental health declining
   - Insufficient mental health providers

2. **Air Quality**: Critical environmental health threat
   - Winter inversions create hazardous conditions
   - PM2.5 and ozone exceedances
   - Disproportionate impact on vulnerable populations

3. **Geographic Health Disparities**: 
   - West side communities disadvantaged
   - 2-3x variation in health outcomes within county

4. **Healthcare Access Gaps**:
   - Uninsured rate above national average
   - Mental health provider shortage
   - Mammography screening below national rate

5. **Housing Affordability**:
   - Median home value 2x national average
   - Growing cost burden concerns

---
